chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Muthanna, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent from her, when should she observe the waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When proof is established for her that she was divorced on a known day and a known month, let her observe the waiting period from the day she was divorced; and if she does not remember which day and which month, let her observe the waiting period from the day the news reaches her.'
ai.seo_question: When does a divorced woman's waiting period begin if her husband is absent and the exact date of divorce is unknown?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural nuances of iddah for absent husbands, emphasizing the necessity of concrete evidence (bayyinah) for precise dating. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty in the timing of the divorce event defers the commencement of the waiting period until the news is formally received, ensuring fairness in legal obligations.
